newsitem.title: USA: Senate majority leader slams Clinton budget.
newsitem.headline: Senate majority leader slams Clinton budget.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's proposed budget raises taxes and fails in his attempt to balance the U.S. budget by 2002 as promised, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Sunday.

Citing an independent analysis, Lott said in a letter to the president and during an appearance on CBS TV that Congressional Budget Office figures would show the budget would be out of balance by $80 billion in 2002 in Clinton's budget were put into effect.

"According to the Joint Committee on Taxation, your budget represents a $13 billion tax increase in 2001 and a $23 billion tax hike over 10 years," Lott said in the letter, signed by the Republican leadership.
The reason, Lott said, is "because your proposed tax increases are permanent, while your proposed tax cuts are only temporary."
